(2) Students going to and from school classes or participating in education activities where such activity is under the immediate supervision and direction of proper school authorities;
(3) A governmental agency acting within the scope of its functions; and
(4) Other activities as provided for by law or regulation.
(Ord. of 11-20-2018(3))
832:
(a) The mayor of the City of Jackson, Georgia, or his or her designee shall administer and enforce the provisions for application for and issuance of permits under this article. The mayor or his or her designee shall have the following duties under this ordinance:
(1) To prepare and provide the necessary forms for the application for a permit and for the submission of any required information needed to properly administer and enforce this article.
(2) To review the application for completeness and to collect a permit licensing fee in the amount to be set by the mayor and council which shall be equal to the administrative costs of processing the permit plus the costs for the use of city services or property, unless the activity is conducted for the sole purpose of public issue speech protected under the First Amendment for which no costs shall be assessed for police protection.
(3) To designate or coordinate sites and set time schedules; to coordinate with county and/or municipal authorities, and, where appropriate, to receive the approval of the state department of transportation or other necessary public officer.
(4) To issue a permit within five days of receipt of an acceptable and complete application.
(b) If any provision of this ordinance provides for the review of an application for a permit by a city officer designated therein, the mayor or his or her designee shall forward a copy of the application to that officer for recommendation.
(c) Upon receipt of the recommendation of the reviewing officer, the mayor shall take action upon the application.
(d) Unless some significant interference with the rights of non-participants exist, or the flow of traffic would unreasonably be obstructed, or the public safety be endangered, or another unreasonable interference with the public welfare, peace, safety, health, good order, and convenience of the general public would occur, the permit shall be granted.
(e) The mayor shall issue a signed permit to an applicant therefore, which permit shall be dated and state the nature and time of the activity authorized.
(Ord. of 11-20-2018(3))
833:
As a condition to issuing a permit, the mayor may require the provision of personnel for trash clean-up of affected areas littered during the activity, the provision of first-aid and medical resources if considered necessary, proof of storage areas for motor vehicles occasioned by the permitted activity, the provision of temporary toilet facilities and other items considered necessary based on experience with such activities, and coordination with other city, county and state officials. The mayor shall not require personnel for normal governmental functions such as traffic control and police protection. Failure to comply with additional necessary requirements of the mayor is grounds for denial of any subsequent permit requested by the private organization or group of private persons and is grounds for a claim for reimbursement of funds expended by the city for such extraordinary expenses agreed to, but not provided by the applicant.
(Ord. of 11-20-2018(3))
834:
If the circumstances are such that a permit application would normally be refused, the mayor in his/her discretion may suggest an alternative route or time.

835:
A permit for a parade, picket line, group demonstration, fundraiser event, or an outdoor group assembly may be revoked for failure to abide by the terms and conditions of the permit or violation of this article or other applicable municipal, state or federal law.
(Ord. of 11-20-2018(3))
836:
Any applicant whose application under this ordinance is denied may appeal such denial to the city council of Jackson, which shall consider such appeal at the next regularly scheduled meeting following the filing of the appeal, if such appeal is filed by the day items are to be placed on the agenda in accordance with the normal procedures of the city council of the City of Jackson. In the event an applicant fails to appeal before the agenda is prepared, he may nevertheless be heard at the next regularly scheduled meeting of the city council if he has provided each councilmember with a copy of the application which he submitted to the mayor and the reasons for denial not less than two business days prior to the regularly scheduled meeting of the mayor and city council following denial of the application. Any appeal shall be filed within 30 days subsequent to denial of the application.

The city council shall determine the cause for denial, and unless possible significant interference with the rights of non-participating citizens, an unreasonable obstruction of the orderly flow of traffic, a clear and present endangerment of Jackson citizens, or another possible specific unreasonable interference with the public welfare, peace, safety, health, good order or convenience of the general public is shown, the permit shall be issued.
(Ord. of 11-20-2018(3))
839:
The purpose of this article is to establish a requirement that all lots within the city be assigned a street number, that the owner or occupant of each residence or other building designed for human use display the appropriate number at a place clearly visible from the public right-of-way and to provide for enforcement of this article and penalties for violations.
(Ord. No. 96-18, 5-21-1996)
840:
The superintendent of the department of public works of the city shall establish a system, with the approval of the city council, which shall provide for the assignment of street numbers for each lot within the city. The owner or occupant of any lot may obtain information concerning the assigned number through the office of the department of public works. If there is any change or modification in the system or the number assigned to any particular lot, those persons affected by the change will be notified within a reasonable time.
(Ord. No. 96-18, art. I(A), 5-21-1996)
841:
The owner and occupant of each lot whereon is located either a residence, a commercial or industrial building or other structure designed for human use shall display the street number of the structure pursuant to the following rules:
(1) The street number will be displayed by use of reflective material which can be easily seen at night when illuminated by a light shone from the public right-of-way.
(2) The individual numbers shall be of a size that will make them easily distinguishable by the eye from the public right-of-way, and each number shall be no less than three inches tall and three inches wide.
(3) On those city lots where the building is set back from the right-of-way and accessed by a driveway leading from the public right-of-way, the street number shall be displayed at the point nearest the public right-of-way beside the main drive leading from the city street, which is the official address of the lot, facing in the direction of the street.
(4) On those lots where the building is at or very near the right-of-way boundary, the street number shall be displayed either on the side of the building or directly in front of the building facing the street which is the official address of the lot.
(5) Display of the street number shall be acceptable, if displayed on a mailbox or at ground level or on a post, if the street number is displayed upon or in front of the lot at curbside and the display otherwise satisfies the requirements of this article as to size, visibility, direction and reflective capability.
(Ord. No. 96-18, art. I(B), 5-21-1996; Ord. No. 99-3, § 1, 5-4-1999)
842:
The department of public works shall periodically inspect to determine whether street numbers are being displayed in compliance with this article. If a lot is found whereon the correct street number is not being displayed in the correct manner, the department of public works may take the following action:
(1) Notice of noncompliance. The superintendent of the department of public works or any employee of the department or any police officer acting upon the authority of the superintendent shall issue a written notice, which shall contain the date of the notice, the correct street address and a description of the deficiency or other noncompliance observed. One copy of such notice shall be either delivered to the occupant at the lot or attached to the building, one copy will be mailed to the owner of record as per the records of the county taxing authority, one copy will be filed with the city clerk and one copy will be kept as part of the records of the department of public works. The notice shall contain an order that the correct street number be properly displayed within ten days from the date of the notice.
(2) Penalty. Failure to correctly display the street number within ten days after the date of the notice shall constitute a violation of this article and shall, upon conviction, subject both the owner and occupant to punishment as provided in section 1-11.
(3) Assessment. If neither the owner nor the occupant comply with the requirement that the street number be properly displayed within ten days following the issuance of a notice as described in subsection (1) of this section, the superintendent of the department of public works may cause the street number to be properly displayed at the expense of the city, and the total cost of such action, including but not limited to materials, labor and reasonable costs of litigation, including attorney's fees, shall be a lien upon the real estate upon which such cost was incurred. Such lien shall attach to the real property upon the filing of an itemized statement of the total sum of the cost by the city clerk in the office of the city clerk on a lien docket maintained for such purposes. Thereafter the lien may be collected by adding same to the cost of any city license fee, city utility bill or other city assessment owed by either the owner or the occupant within a period of seven years after the date of filing of the lien. No deposit for city utilities may be refunded on property upon which such a lien exists, until the lien is paid in full. No city utility services may commence for property upon which such a lien exists, until the lien is paid in full. Also, the lien may be collected by direct litigation against either the owner or the occupant, filed in the name of the city, and the city would be entitled to recover not only the amount of the lien, but any cost of court or other reasonable litigation expense, including attorney's fees, necessary for the enforcement of the lien.
(Ord. No. 96-18, art. I(C), 5-21-1996)

855:
The city shall provide and be responsible for the construction, establishment, maintenance, and operation of lighting fixtures and lighting components for the illumination of public street, roads, sidewalks, and alleyways (hereinafter sometimes referred to collectively as "public right-of-ways" or "PRW") situated within the incorporated area of the city that also fall within the electric territory for Jackson Electric in the manner and in accordance with the standards set forth in this article.
For all public right-of-ways within the incorporated areas of the city that fall outside of the Jackson Electric territory, the construction, establishment and maintenance of the lighting fixtures and lighting components are the responsibility of the developer or provider within a given territory but must be done in accordance with the standards set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999; Ord. No. 2023-022, 6-20-2023)
856:
(a) The Jackson Electric Department or zoning administrator or such other person or department as may be designated by the city council from time to time shall be responsible for administering the street lighting program as set forth in this article and shall:
(1) Acknowledge and work in accordance with the electric territories as defined by the State of Georgia; and
(2) Notify any developer, builder, planner, or other individual or agency of the requirements of this article; and
(3) Review all permits to install lights within the public right of way for accuracy and compliance with the standards of this article; and
(4) Establish an orderly system of numbering street lighting districts (which may be in accordance with the tax assessor or tax commissioner); and
(5) Ensure that whoever is responsible for the construction and installation of all street lighting poles securely fastens a number to each pole that is visible from the street level; and
(6) Perform any and all acts or duties necessary or proper for the attainment of the purposes herein set out.
(b) Outside the Jackson Electric territory, constructing and installing streetlights and lighting fixtures and lighting components within the public right of ways by other individuals and entities other than Jackson Electric shall adhere to the following:
(1) Installation requires a permit from the city; and
(2) Construction, installation, and maintenance must comply with the standards of the city; and
(3) City of Jackson is only responsible for the energy usage, not the maintenance or consumable components.
(c) Installation of lights outside of the public right-of-ways on parcels within the city limits:
(1) When a customer is required by code or on their own elects to install lights outside of the city right-of-ways, the construction, establishment, and installation of lighting fixtures and lighting components are the responsibility of the developer; and
(2) The energy usage for all lighting fixtures and lighting components, temporary or permanent, are the responsibility of the developer, property owner, tenant, or their designee.
(d) Public streets within a residential subdivision or commercial/industrial park:
(1) Within a subdivision, commercial or industrial park, streetlights are required and must be in accordance with the standards of the city, this article, and other electric department rules and regulations; and
(2) Within the public right of ways on city streets within subdivisions or commercial/industrial parks, the construction, establishment, and installation of lighting fixtures and lighting components are the responsibility of the developer; and
(3) All lights must be approved by the city and require an approved preliminary plat. Specifications for fixtures and poles will be approved during the process. Any lights installed inside the city right of way without city approval, or out of compliance with city standards will be subject to corrective action at the expense of the developer or landowner.
(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999; Ord. No. 2023-022, 6-20-2023)
859:
The owner or owners of residential lots within either an existing subdivision or a discrete and definable area, or the owner or owners of property lying within an area zoned for purposes other than residential use, may submit to the community development director, for approval, a petition for the creation of a street lighting district wherein lighting fixtures for the illumination of public rights-of-way shall be installed and operated. The petition must contain the signatures of at least 66 percent of the owners of the property lying within the proposed street lighting district in favor of such designation and must contain an accurate description of the property to be included by tax map parcel numbers as the same are used by the county tax assessor and the county tax commissioner. The community development director shall, within 60 days from the date of approval of the petition, submit such petition to the city council for final approval. In the event 100 percent of the owners within any such proposed district shall fail to sign such petition, a notice of a public hearing to be conducted by the city council shall first be published in the newspaper in which the city advertisements are usually published at least 15 days and no more than 45 days preceding the meeting at which the city council shall consider the creation of a street lighting district.
(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999)
860:
(a) The owner or owners of property lying within a proposed subdivision of land may, but shall not be required to, construct and install lighting fixtures for illumination of public rights-of-way to be located within such proposed subdivision, subject to the provisions of this article. A written request for authorization to construct and install lighting fixtures signed by all owners of such property shall be submitted to the community development director on such forms as may be prescribed, from time to time, by the community development director together with plans and specifications for such lighting fixtures for approval by the community development director. Such plans and specifications shall be designed and/or approved by the public utility company which will provide electrical service to the proposed subdivision and shall include, but not be limited to, a preliminary plat of the proposed subdivision showing the location of the lighting fixtures within the subdivision as required by the appropriate public utility, and a description of the fixtures, poles, and other components approved for use by such utility company. Upon approval of the plans and specifications by the community development director, such plans, specifications, and other required documents, together with the recommendation of the community development director, shall be submitted to the city council for final approval. The construction and installation of such lighting fixtures shall not commence until: (i) the city council has approved such plans and specifications; and (ii) the city planning and zoning commission has approved the preliminary plat of the proposed subdivision.
(b) In the event the community development director denies the request by such owner or owners for authorization to construct and install such lighting fixtures, the community development director shall notify such owner or owners in writing of such denial and the reasons therefor. Any such owner or owners shall have the right to appeal the decision of the community development director by filing a written notice of appeal with the community development director within 30 days from the date of said notice of denial. The community development director shall thereupon submit the notice of appeal to the city council together with all plans, specifications and other documents constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken for placement upon the agenda of the city council for its determination. The city council may reserve or affirm, in whole or in part, or may modify the decision from which the appeal is taken.
(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999)
861:
Any other provision of this article to the contrary notwithstanding, the city council shall be authorized and empowered to create special street lighting districts and provide lighting fixtures in areas in which the city council has determined that special conditions exist which uniquely affect such areas so as to warrant the creation of such districts and the provision of such lighting fixtures therein. In making such determination, the special conditions which the city council may consider shall include, but not limited to, public safety, security and welfare, and the creation of such street lighting districts shall be upon such terms and conditions and in such manner as the city council may deem necessary or proper. (Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999)
864:
(a) The cost of providing and maintaining service in street lighting districts created pursuant to this article shall be the actual cost of the energy used plus the retirement of any construction costs incurred in the installation of lighting fixtures and an amount equal to 20 percent of such sum to cover administrative expenses. 866:

(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999)
869:
The American National Standard Practice of Roadway Lighting of the Illuminating Engineering Society, as approved by the American Standards Institute, as amended from time to time, is hereby adopted as the standard for the installation and operation of lighting in the incorporated area of the city, with the following exceptions:
(1) Lighting fixtures installed within public rights-of-way to be operated for the purpose of street illumination shall comply with these standards. The minimum average horizontal footcandle illumination level by roadway classification shall be:
_____
Roadway Classification | Commercial Area | Intermediate Area | Residential Area
Major | 2.0 | 1.2 | 0.9
Collector | 1.2 | 0.9 | 0.6
Local or Residential | 0.9 | 0.6 | 0.2
_____
The uniformity of illumination shall be such that the point of lowest illumination shall have at least one-third of the average horizontal footcandle required illumination level except that on local or residential streets, it may not be less than one-sixth of this average.
(b) Lighting fixtures installed within public rights-of-way as "security lights" or for the purpose of lighting areas other than streets shall be mounted on the side of the pole opposite from the street and shall be oriented in such a manner to insure that the lateral light distribution, at the initial light source, is perpendicular to the street, so as to protect the users of the street from objectionable glare.
(c) Lighting fixtures installed within or outside of public rights-of-way for any other purpose shall be installed and operated in such a manner to prevent glare from being a hazard to or interfering with the normal use of public rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. 99-10, 2-11-1999)

887:
For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms are defined. Unless specifically defined, words or phrases used in this chapter shall be interpreted to have the meaning in common usage and to give this chapter the most reasonable application.
Apartment: means a unit within a building consisting of two units or more for rent.
Building means a structure having a roof supported by columns or walls for the shelter, support or enclosure of persons, animals, or equipment and requiring a separate power meter to be installed for the building to have electrical service. This will also include mobile homes or manufactured homes. For the purposes of this chapter, the term "building" may also include other manmade structures meeting the same requirement as in the first sentence.
City council means the City of Jackson, Georgia City Council.
Condominium means an ownership of a single unit within a structure that may include common areas and facilities.
Honorary road name means a secondary road name designated to an individual person or organization.

Official road name means the name as designated in the complete list of all roads in the City of Jackson, Georgia.
Private road means any road, which is not maintained by the Georgia Department of Transportation, Butts County and/or the City of Jackson, Georgia through the use of public funds.

Such roads may be of various types including frontage roads, rear access roads, roads with cul-de-sac and dead-end roads. This definition includes secondary roads, but does not include driveways. For purposes of this chapter, road and street shall have the same meaning.

(Ord. of 8-3-2021, § I)
888:
The naming of roads shall be reviewed and approved by the city council per the selection standards provided in this article.
(Ord. of 8-3-2021, § I)
889:
The following standards will be used in consideration of new or proposed road names. All current roads that would otherwise not meet these standards will be granted exceptions and maintain those names until changes, if considered, can be made to conform to this chapter.
(1) Names of new roads or proposed changes must not duplicate, in wording, in sound or pronunciation, an existing road within the City of Jackson, Georgia regardless of distance between occurrences or in address ranges/block numbers.
(2) Road names may not contain abbreviations of words, names or initials.
(3) Names of individuals will only be permitted for honorary purposes unless the individual holds a state, national or local significance. Any honorary designation shall be subject to subsection 50-261 of this chapter.
(4) Single alphabetical characters are prohibited.
(5) Road names must be easy to pronounce and easily recognizable in emergency situations.
(6) Special characters will not be permitted: periods, dashes, apostrophes, hyphens, etc.
(7) Names that may be offensive (slang, words with double-meanings, etc.) will not be allowed.
(8) Road names will be continuous throughout their entire length, when feasible.
(9) Names which have homonyms (i.e., other words pronounced similarly but spelled differently) should not be used on any street and certainly not on multiple streets even if the street type is different (e.g., Steven Lane/Stephen Lane; Disk Drive/Disc Lane).
(Ord. of 8-3-2021, § I)

(a) A request for road name reservation can be presented to the city council for any new planned development. These road names will be reviewed and reserved, if approved.

894:
Whenever a change to an approved and addressed road name is requested by a property owner or developer with access to the subject road, the following procedures shall apply.
(1) A complete application shall be made with the City of Jackson, which shall be accompanied by a petition signed by 66 percent (two-thirds) or more of the property owners adjoining the said road in agreement. (An adjoining property owner is one who owns an interest in property contiguous to the street.) A nonrefundable application fee of $250.00 must be submitted to the City of Jackson prior to processing; provided, however, applications initiated by city staff will have no fees associated with them.
(2) Within 30 days of submittal, the city will determine the percentage of the affected property owners that have signed the petition. If less than 66 percent of the affected property owners have signed the petition, it will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant. If 66 percent or more have signed, the department will review the proposed road name for compliance with the requirements of this article.
(3) If the proposed road name meets all criteria provided in the selection standards itemized in this article, the proposed road name will be "reserved." A letter will then be sent by the City of Jackson to affected city and county departments for review and comments. If the requested name change receives any unfavorable comments, the City of Jackson will schedule a meeting with affected departments and agencies to develop recommendations as to the beginning and ending points of said change (if necessary), or name change, or any road number changes that may be applicable.
(4) After review and acceptance by the city and county departments of the request, and if 66 percent or more of the affected property owners have signed a petition, then the proposal will be placed on the agenda of the city council. If all of the affected property owners do not agree to the requested road name change, or if less than 100 percent have signed the petition, then an advertised public hearing before the city council will be scheduled and held. Note, however, that at least 66 percent of the affected property owners must sign the petition for it to be accepted for processing.
(5) A notice advertising the name change shall be required to be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the city at least 15 days, but not more than 45 days, before the public hearing.
(6) If, after public hearing, the name change is approved by the city council, then all relevant city and county departments will make changes as necessary and again notify affected property owners and public agencies in writing at least ten days before the change becomes effective.
(7) The applicant for road name change that has been approved shall be responsible for revising any final plats and paying any associated fees. The applicant shall also be responsible for the cost of new road name signs that will replace existing road name signs.
(Ord. of 8-3-2021, § I)
